paras: Today I woke up strange. As if my body were rented, and I an intruder. A foreign body.
My heart was not mine. I only carried it.
And how I trembled before lucidity. It was my greatest horror. I would have given anything not to lodge it. But even so it scratched at the walls of my head.
Lucidity made my heart a burden. A bag of flesh on my back. And the more I dragged it, the heavier the trail grew, of earth, of gravel, of ground.
The more I think about what makes me, me. The less I understand of that substance.
I know I feel more than I can bear. But my flesh draws borders too far for me to reach.
And I lock myself inside out. I have no house. I am a host.
A true parasite.
I lie down warm, but slowly I go cold. And even when winter ends. And the cold leaves me. I hold on to its cloak. I forbid it to go.
I spread its needles over my body. And in the shiver of each puncture, I warm myself.
I make the ice cover the sun. Until the light goes cold. Leaving only preserved flesh.
But it does not obey me. It slips through my fingers.
It rejects me.
And inside this flesh there is earth. Where worms feed in the womb of death.
They make mud where I sink. It is my ecosystem.
A liquid shadow that seeps into the soil and lets nothing grow.
And when my throat vibrates in the vacuum like the string of a satanic guitar.
Words I will never be able to say pursue me. Something is being lost. Getting farther away.
And amnesia seduces me, makes me drowsy.
Makes my eyes close inside me.
I was expelled from my body. From where I suck life.
Suiciding the man for the boy. I abandon the truth.
I abandon myself.
I spend my days locked in my room. watching my flesh blend into the walls.
Tears run down the peeling paint.
There is no outside. There is only hunger. In a greenish dark.
And the hyenas, crocodiles and vultures feed there. But my blood has already dried. Still they bite.
They cut the fibres so as not to forget. Sinking their fangs until they die, until they forget.
Hunger will win.

Under the blanket for two eternities. I wake without getting up. Crucified on the bed. There is no heaven. There is only hell, high up. The bed opens its mouth, and the pillow bites. Pierces my skull, which leaks a tasteless liquid.
All the vertebrae, viscera and ribs are a pile of parts that do not work.
And my heart does not beat, it coughs.
The drool builds up, poisoning all the calm that only the lonely know.
The disease I contracted in the womb has no remedy, but with each day that passes I walk toward a cure.
I let the shadow walk ahead of me. Let my feet court the dark.
And at this crossroads, I meet Satan in the middle of the road, having lost his way. We walk hand in hand, toward the cure.
The coffin is my bed. It is the cross I hesitate to call mine. But I lie down with open arms.
A crack comes to deceive the light. It refracts from afar in a sombre immensity like a shy little girl. Scratch the wood's entrails! try! But I am so thirsty that I drink thirst.
Thirst is my water.
The head tries to rise, the body will not let it. They tear the dark matter.
Half is death, the other too.
I am leaking. Leaking out of myself. I am not a human thing. I am a broth. A thin broth. Two. None. Kneaded from a substance of mine, but unknown. Seeping into myself.
I dig to fit, to the sound of footsteps from the world above. They follow something I cannot follow.
And when the sound of the footsteps drifts off to sleep. I am afraid to close my eyes. Here where stars die, and space stretches. The light is limp. It is the portrait of a hole.
And nothing touches nothing.
And it is no longer I who acts. I live inside an idea. A stitch in the lobe of the corpse.
That suture is the only thing that binds me to the rightful owner.

And when the earth pulses. Swallowing a thin longing. I miss missing. But the memory is white. It is strange. Borrowed from another whom I fear. The remembrance comes in the small hours while my hair fuses with the threads of the mattress, and moans near me like an animal in heat.
While he sleeps, I can see the dark. And try to reach something that was coming slowly.
But he wakes, before I arrive. And I no longer see.
I see nothing.
Not even nothing.
The addiction to oxygen leaves me breathless. The dead breeze I swallow dry makes the still wind thick.
A translucent poison.
And this time I caress fingers soaked in delirium. Delirium sucks my soul. I can dry out, stop the seepage.

I bite lips full of trickery. I drain the drool with a kiss on my face. Until nothing makes a word anymore. Delirium made, out of nothing, a something. And how delicious is the tender flesh of a ghost.

But my hunger is not sated. It deforms my brain. Bends my nerves. Makes me eat the remains of an insect. It fell into my mouth while I slept. Dove into a deep dark. Its larvae will die soon. What guilt would I feel? But I do. Faced with the absolute rot I cannot not feel. I ate an insect. Crushed it between my teeth, swallowed its slime, and finally, I tasted.

And today I fall in love with ugliness. I never understood why others are so afraid of it. Ugliness is not ugly. If loving were beautiful, beautiful would be ugly. To love something is grotesque. It is beautiful. It is in ugliness that I find love. And I am not afraid. I have passion. In an immensity of horror. I love being horrible. I smile with yellow teeth, and drink from a dirty spring. I drink ugly. And even if no one loves me, I choose ugliness. An ugly thing, but one I recognise.
There is something divine in the ugly. Like a sharp dark.
And everything that was new became a little less new. I am afraid nothing recent will be left. That I will become the sterile past of parents and children.
But a lucid dream ends too. And one day the friction of the air warmed my face.
For the first time my forehead scraped the asphalt that before only my feet had touched.
Before, I did not bleed. Not a drop. But everything changed with you.
I stuffed crumbs of my spirit. Of malnourished dough. Into the mouth of my parasite sister. We dined in the dry womb, soaked in discharge.
When I cut off my arm and handed it to you. You slid the severed flesh between your thighs. For each finger of mine to take on an extremity of yours.
And you tore a whisper from my ear, as if it had never left your throat:
"Tonight I want you to crawl across the room, to my bed, and wrap yourself around my skin like a sheet.
And then, little brother, I will nurse you like a baby of blood, and let you bite until you choke."
Only you were able to ease the crown that crushed me. I, of all people, who bit only to wear down my teeth, rubbed my tongue between your molars, addicted to the white slime.
And even if something was lost. I found it. You found it.
I understood how a soul stretches.
And the whole world will die without discovering what it is to love me.
Except you, who ate this strange flesh.
But we sang our dead tongue, inherited from ancestral silence. Strings wounded the sterile wood, and our calluses fused living flesh with mad words, in a cannibal choir.
Where did the violin end? Where did the piano begin? We composed the score of our extinction.
And all we could do was bow hand in hand for a curtain to decapitate, and Death to applaud.

One day the flowers withered on the grave. The trampled grass turned to sludge and not even the footprint could be seen. The headstone was swallowed. And drops erased the epitaph of a promise. Of the lie they told the salted soil.
Two holes do not fill.
From a time pregnant with pleasure, a soft yolk was born.
How can the weight of nothing be so hard to carry?
And this weight slowly spread through my whole body, as if I had lain down wrong. And even the silence seemed quieter.
If I opened my chest, I would still see you there. But I would see you slipping away.
Now my face is cold. You went.
And I have no solitude. I am solitude. We are one flesh. Wherever I go, she waits for me.
When I sleep, she wraps me in icy fingers. When I wake, she reminds me of what I wanted to forget. Even among them, the bride who stayed dresses me like a wet veil.
Death sings at our ceremony. I dance in the ashes of a star. Until my feet bleed — I do not stop, I cannot stop.
I fall in love with mourning. And my love dissects the corpse of a ghost. Bathes in ancestral liquid.
My knees pierce the ground, trying to extract the inheritance of a promise.
But still I dance.
Pain is my foreign body. My common place. Where the light bleeds in the placenta of a shadow.
Only dark is space.
And I can no longer live so far from my body.
I made Me.
